fact: 1923年9月1日11时58分32秒（日本标准时间），日本关东地方发生矩震级7.9—8.2的大型逆冲地震，震中位于相模湾内、东京西南约100公里处，震源深度约23公里。地震持续约4分48秒，现代研究认为由三分钟内连续三次主要震动组成：神奈川县下的初始逆冲地震，三分钟后东京湾下方7.2级地震，再两分钟后山梨县7.3级地震。东京超过一半、横滨几乎全部被毁，约250万人无家可归。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Great Kantō Earthquake
sources.quote: The Great Kantō Earthquake was a megathrust earthquake that struck the Kantō Plain on the main Japanese island of Honshu at 11:58:32 JST (02:58:32 UTC) on Saturday, 1 September 1923. It had an approximate magnitude of 8.0 on the moment magnitude scale (Mw), with its epicenter located some 100 km (62 mi) southwest of the capital Tokyo. ... Over half of Tokyo and nearly all of Yokohama were destroyed, leaving approximately 2.5 million people homeless.

sources.title: 百度百科，关东大地震
sources.quote: 1923年9月1日,在日本的横滨和东京一带发生直下型特大地震,震源位于相模湾内,受灾区域包括神奈川、千叶、静冈和山梨等地。其最初测定震级为7.9级,于1996年修正为8.1级,造成10.5万人死亡。

fact: 地震死亡与失踪人数估计在10.5万至14万人之间。其中建筑倒塌死亡约1.1万人，火灾死亡约9.2万人，其他次生灾害约0.2万人。东京本所被服厂旧址（陆军被服厂）的空地上约4万人避难时遭遇火龙卷，几乎全部遇难。横滨90%以上建筑被毁。火灾因台风强风而迅速蔓延，是造成大多数伤亡的原因。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Great Kantō Earthquake
sources.quote: The death toll is estimated to have been between 105,000 and 140,000 people, including tens of thousands who went missing and were presumed dead. Over half of Tokyo and nearly all of Yokohama were destroyed. ... Fires, exacerbated by strong winds from a nearby typhoon, spread rapidly through the densely populated urban areas, accounting for the majority of the devastation and casualties.

sources.title: 百度百科，关东大地震
sources.quote: 造成10.5万人死亡,其中由于建筑倒塌造成的死亡人数为1.1万人,地震引发火灾造成9.2万人死亡,其他次生灾害造成0.2万人死亡。

fact: 1923年9月2日，日本政府发布戒严令，社会秩序由军队、警察和自警团协同维持。9月12日，摄政皇太子裕仁发布诏书，要求「不仅恢复城市到原有状态，还要为未来发展提供条件、让城市面貌焕然一新」。9月27日，帝都复兴院成立，内务大臣后藤新平兼任总裁。

sources.title: 百度百科，关东大地震
sources.quote: 日本政府于1923年9月2日发布戒严令,社会秩序由军队、警察和自警团协同维持。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Great Kantō Earthquake
sources.quote: On 12 September, Regent Hirohito issued an imperial rescript calling for "not only to restore the city to its previous state, but also to allow for future developments and to provide the city with a renewed appearance."

fact: 【关东大地震后的谣言骚乱与屠杀——真实历史事件】地震后混乱中，「朝鲜人在水井投毒」「要放火烧火药库」「破坏桥梁」「趁地震暴动」等谣言四处流传。在军方、警察和市民自警团的煽动与执行下，发生了对朝鲜人和中国人的大规模屠杀事件。据研究数据，超过6000名朝鲜居民和近800名中国居民遇难。遇难中国人为劳工和留学生共约700—750人，其中包括周恩来留日时的好友王希天。当时日本内务省的官方统计仅记录231名朝鲜人被杀、3名中国人和59名日本人被当成朝鲜人误杀，与研究数据差距极大。1923年10月日本政府起诉参与屠杀的自警团成员，但无人受到重判，其中仅8人因杀害华人被起诉，最高刑罚为有期徒刑2年、缓刑2年。1924年日本政府提出赔偿方案，但至今未实施。

sources.title: China Daily, Memorial remembers Korean, Chinese massacre victims
sources.quote: In the confusion caused by the quake, rumors spread that Koreans had "poisoned wells". Afterwards, nearly 800 Chinese residents and over 6,000 Korean residents in Japan fell victim to massacres orchestrated by Japanese military, law enforcement and nationalist extremists, according to research data. ... In 1924, the Japanese government proposed a compensation plan, which, however, has not been implemented to this day.

sources.title: 鹤壁日报（转引环球时报），93年前日本地震后「朝鲜人向井里投毒」谣言引发一场杀戮
sources.quote: 共约700名中国劳工和留学生在这场屠杀中遇难,其中包括周恩来当年留日时的好友王希天。在这场疯狂而荒唐的大屠杀中,约有六七千名朝鲜人遇难。但当时日本内务省的统计显示,仅231名朝鲜人被杀,另有3名中国人和59名日本人被当成朝鲜人误杀。当年10月,日本政府对参与屠杀的「自警团」成员进行起诉,但无人受到重判,其中仅有8人因杀害华人而被起诉,最高刑罚则是有期徒刑2年,缓刑2年。

sources.title: 新华社日本频道，関東大震災朝鮮人・中国人虐殺103年
sources.quote: 中国人労働者、留学生750人以上と朝鮮人労働者6千人以上が犠牲となった惨劇は「関東大震災時の中国人・朝鮮人虐殺」として知られている。1924年、日本政府は賠償案を策定したが、今日に至るまで履行されていない。

fact: 后藤新平领导的帝都复兴院提出复兴计划：最初方案预算约30亿日元（超过当时整个国家预算的两倍），遭大藏大臣井上准之助和内阁强烈反对。复兴审议会将预算削减到5.97亿日元，帝国议会1923年12月进一步削减到4.68亿日元。土地整理（区画整理）在1923年12月《特别都市规划法》授权下实施，政府可无偿征收高达10%的私有土地；东京约3000万平方米土地划入66个整理区。最终复兴支出约7.44亿日元。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Great Kantō Earthquake
sources.quote: Gotō Shinpei, as Home Minister and head of the Reconstruction Institute (Teito fukkōin), championed ambitious and expensive plans, initially proposing a budget of ¥3 billion—more than twice the entire national budget at the time. ... Gotō's plans were progressively scaled back, with the budget reduced to ¥597 million by the council and further to ¥468 million by the Diet in December 1923. ... The Special Urban Planning Law of December 1923 empowered the government to rationalize irregular land plots, widen streets, and create public spaces by confiscating up to 10 percent of private land without monetary compensation. Roughly 30,000,000 square meters of land in Tokyo were divided into 66 readjustment districts. ... The final reconstruction expenditure by national and city governments totaled roughly ¥744 million.

sources.title: 东京都都市整备局，Reconstruction following the Great Kanto Earthquake
sources.quote: Although the budget for the government plan, which originally called for 1.5 billion yen, was cut to 468.44 million yen, the plan achieved results such as being the first to incorporate modern city planning methods.

fact: 地震后金融活动立即停滞，政府发布紧急敕令实行票据延期偿付（moratorium）。东京市约73.4%的家庭受灾，约3465公顷（占城区面积44%）被大火烧毁。国际援助从美国、英国和亚洲各地运抵横滨受损的港口。大量居民从东京市中心迁往郊区，出现「灾害甜甜圈现象」。

sources.title: 百度百科英文版，Kantō Great Earthquake of 1923
sources.quote: Financial activities stalled immediately after the earthquake, leading to an emergency Imperial Ordinance for payment postponement. ... many people relocated from the city center of Tokyo to the suburbs due to the disaster, leading to the occurrence of the "doughnut phenomenon caused by natural disasters".

sources.title: 东京都都市整备局，Reconstruction following the Great Kanto Earthquake
sources.quote: About 73.4 percent of households in the city of Tokyo were affected by the disaster, and approximately 3,465 hectares, or 44 percent of the city's area, was destroyed by the great fires triggered by the quake.

fact: 1923年9月2日戒严令发布后，军队和警察拥有广泛的治安维持权。在谣言骚乱中，军队、警察和自警团协同参与了对朝鲜人和中国人的搜捕与屠杀。地震后政府为控制霍乱流行也实施了军事管制。地震保险条款通常不覆盖此类特大自然灾害；政府提出按保额10%补贴保险赔付的方案未通过议会，农商大臣�的场健二郎因此辞职。

sources.title: 百度百科，关东大地震
sources.quote: 日本政府于1923年9月2日发布戒严令,社会秩序由军队、警察和自警团协同维持。地震后,有关朝鲜人纵火、投毒、暴动的谣言四处流传,其中也夹杂着部分有关中国人暴动的蜚语,军队、警察和市民在谣言煽动下制造屠杀事件。

sources.title: Rienner, From Party Politics to Militarism in Japan, 1924–1941
sources.quote: Another point of contention in the Diet was the problem of earthquake insurance. Normal insurance policies stipulated that damages incurred from major natural disasters such as earthquakes of this magnitude would not be covered. But the government wanted to provide subsidies that would allow insurance claims to be paid at a rate of 10 percent of the total. This, too, did not pass the Diet, and as a result Minister of Agriculture and Commerce Den Kenjirō resigned.

fact: 震灾复兴融资以外债为主：1931年J.P.摩根公司承销了超过10亿日元的震灾复兴债券，金额超过当时日本国家预算的60%。复兴支出约一半用于电力行业（当时正处于引入火电的阶段）。1924年大藏大臣井上准之助在巨大压力下才同意发行公债融资复兴。震灾后日本经济环境持续恶化，从1927年昭和金融恐慌到1930年解除金禁令和大萧条，对日本经济造成重大冲击。

sources.title: 百度百科英文版，Kantō Great Earthquake of 1923
sources.quote: A significant amount of foreign debt was injected into the reconstruction work, with roughly half of the expenditure going towards the power industry, which was at a stage of introducing thermal power generation. In 1931 (Shōwa 6), J.P. Morgan & Co. underwrote over 1 billion yen in earthquake reconstruction bonds, an amount exceeding 60% of Japan's national budget at the time.

sources.title: Asian Studies, The Great Kantō Earthquake of 1923 and the Japanese Nation
sources.quote: Inoue refused to raise new taxes for Tokyo's reconstruction and, in 1924, only after considerable pressure, agreed to release public bonds to finance reconstruction.

fact: 复兴计划实施后，东京道路总面积增加45%，主要干道（昭和通、靖国通）建成，永代桥、清洲桥等现代钢桥跨越隅田川。土地整理在东京被烧毁面积的约90%（约3117公顷）范围内推行。1930年3月复兴正式庆祝时，东京的城市面貌已发生显著变化。复兴规划首次引入现代城市规划方法，对日本战后复兴规划也产生影响。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Great Kantō Earthquake
sources.quote: The total area of roads in Tokyo increased by 45 percent, and many were widened and paved, with modern sidewalks. Key arterial roads like Shōwa-dōri and Yasukuni-dōri were constructed, and new, modern steel bridges, such as the Eitai-bashi and Kiyosu-bashi spanning the Sumida River, became icons of the new city.

sources.title: 东京都都市整备局，Reconstruction following the Great Kanto Earthquake
sources.quote: the plan achieved results such as being the first to incorporate modern city planning methods. Years later, it even had an impact on Japan's postwar reconstruction plan. ... land readjustment put into motion by the reconstruction project was carried out extensively by the national government and the city of Tokyo over approximately 90 percent of the area destroyed by fire in Tokyo, or just over 3,117 hectares of land.
